//: Machine profile: MacBook — fallback machine. The Mac mini is the single
source of truth for agent memory (see mac-mini.json); this machine pulls
on connect and pushes debounced snapshots via `watch`.
remoteUrl is the bare git repo on the mini, reached over the `mini` SSH
host alias (configure it in ~/.ssh/config, e.g. HostName + User +
IdentityFile). The `~` in 'mini:~/memory-sync/pandora-memory.git' is
expanded by the remote shell over ssh — that is normal scp-like git
remote syntax and requires no local expansion.
repositorySubdir MUST be identical across every machine sharing this
remote — it is the ONLY thing that determines the remote tree path
(see toRepositoryRelativePath in src/memory-sync/config.ts: remote path
= path.posix.join(repositorySubdir, <syncPaths destination + relative
path>)). It used to be set to 'macbook' here and 'mac-mini' in
mac-mini.json — that made the two machines write to two separate
top-level trees in the same bare repo and never see each other's
pushes (a live cross-machine E2E test caught this: mini `pull` after a
MacBook `push` reported applied=0). Both profiles now use the same
'pandora' value. The 'profile' field below is a DIFFERENT, unrelated
setting — it only names this machine's LOCAL state directory
(queue/base/tmp under stateDir); it is safe for it to differ per
machine (and it does: 'macbook' here, 'mac-mini' there) precisely
because it never touches the remote.
syncPaths is a single directory entry covering the ENTIRE rootDir
(source '.'), so every file agent-memory-sync finds there is synced —
the real Claude Code memory directory holds ~236 flat .md files with no
daily/ or logs/ subdirectories; the previous syncPaths (a literal
'MEMORY.md' file plus nonexistent daily/logs directories) missed all of
them. destination is the non-'.' literal 'memory', not '.': a bare '.'
destination round-trips through push but is silently unmappable on
pull/restore (mapRemotePathToLocalAbsolute's directory-prefix match
needs a real path segment, not '.' — verified empirically, see the
implementer's task notes / git history for this fix). A single
directory root also naturally covers any future subdirectories without
further changes.
stateDir is set OUTSIDE rootDir (a separate ~/.agent-memory-sync tree,
not '<rootDir>/.agent-memory-sync/...'), which matters now that
syncPaths covers the whole rootDir: if stateDir stayed nested inside
rootDir, syncPaths' recursive walk would also pick up this tool's own
internal git working copies/queue/base snapshots and try to sync them
as if they were memory content. An absolute stateDir value overrides
the rootDir-relative default entirely (path.resolve treats an absolute
second argument as authoritative) — see resolveRunConfig() in
src/config/loader.ts.
Namespace divergence (read before copying this file to another machine):
Claude Code derives its per-project memory slug from the absolute path
of the project working directory, including the OS username. On this
MacBook the repo lives at /Users/lan/git/pandora, so Claude Code stores
memory under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-lan-git-pandora/memory — hence
the hardcoded rootDir below. On the Mac mini the OS user differs
(lannguyensi), so the SAME repository checkout path pattern yields a
DIFFERENT slug: -Users-lannguyensi-git-pandora (see mac-mini.json). The
two machines' local memory directories are intentionally NOT named the
same; only the remote (repositorySubdir 'pandora') and the shared bare
repo are common ground.
rootDir/stateDir intentionally use resolved absolute paths rather than
'~': agent-memory-sync's config loader does not perform shell-style
tilde expansion (path.resolve('~/x') resolves '~' as a literal path
segment, not the home directory) — see src/config/loader.ts
resolveRunConfig(). Adjust the /Users/lan prefix if you copy this
profile to a machine with a different OS username.
Activation: pass BOTH --config (this file) and the 'macbook' profile
argument, e.g. `agent-memory-sync run macbook --config profiles/macbook.json`.
The CLI's [profile] positional argument always defaults to 'default' and
overrides this file's 'profile' field when omitted, so state files
(queue/, base/, tmp/) land under the intended profile subdirectory only
if the positional argument is passed explicitly too. See docs/machine-setup.md.
